patch_description: The best prior result (total_cost 1035.14) came from plain Dijkstra per destination, while naive reuse-based Steiner routing degraded cost (1618.37) because forced trunk reuse inflated per-destination path lengths. The new algorithm keeps the Dijkstra baseline but adds a cost-aware Steiner improvement: destinations are processed in descending order of baseline path cost (so expensive routes build shared trunks first), and each destination's route is chosen only if its reuse-discounted path is at least as cheap as its baseline Dijkstra path (safety_margin parameter ensures we never route worse than the baseline). This guarantees the result is never worse than the best-known baseline while opportunistically exploiting shared trunks and multi-network parallel routes to cut cost further.
